_meta.indication: IBSRELA is indicated for treatment of irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) in adults.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized 1:1, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with a 12-week treatment period followed by a 4-week randomized withdrawal period.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults (18 to 75 years old) with constipation-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-C).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects who were weekly overall responders at 6 or more of the first 12 weeks (6/12 weeks overall responder rate), requiring both CSBM and abdominal pain response criteria met in the same week.
pivotal_trials.n: 606 patients randomized 1:1 to tenapanor or placebo (ITT 307 tenapanor / 299 placebo).
pivotal_trials.result: Overall responder rate 27.0% (83/307) tenapanor vs 18.7% (56/299) placebo; difference 8.3% (95% CI 1.7%, 15.0%), p=0.020.

nct_ctgov.title: A 12-Week Study With a 4-Week Randomized Withdrawal Period to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Tenapanor for the Treatment of IBS-C

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized 1:1, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with a 26-week double-blind parallel-group treatment period.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults (18 to 75 years old) with constipation-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-C).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects who were weekly overall responders at 6 or more of the first 12 weeks (6/12 weeks overall responder rate).
pivotal_trials.result: Overall responder rate 36.5% (107/293) tenapanor vs 23.7% (71/300) placebo; difference 12.9% (95% CI 5.5%, 20.2%), p<0.001.

nct_ctgov.title: A 26-Week Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Tenapanor in IBS-C

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=2%) are diarrhea, abdominal distension, flatulence and dizziness. Diarrhea was the most common AE (16% vs 4% placebo in Trial 1, 26 weeks); severe diarrhea occurred in 2.5% of IBSRELA-treated patients vs 0.2% placebo. Discontinuations for diarrhea occurred in 6.5% vs 0.7% placebo.
target_moa: Tenapanor is a first-in-class, locally acting inhibitor of the sodium/hydrogen exchanger 3 (NHE3), an antiporter on the apical surface of the small intestine and colon primarily responsible for absorption of dietary sodium; inhibition increases intestinal fluid.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: RISK OF SERIOUS DEHYDRATION IN PEDIATRIC PATIENTS — IBSRELA is contraindicated in patients less than 6 years of age; in young juvenile rats, tenapanor caused deaths presumed to be due to dehydration. Avoid use in patients 6 to less than 12 years of age.

rems.type: A REMS will not be required.

summary.text: Standard review NDA received 09/12/2018 with a PDUFA goal date of 09/12/2019; approved on a traditional (full) approval basis supported by two adequate and well-controlled phase 3 trials, without accelerated approval or expedited-program designations.

citations.quote: Tenapanor was demonstrated to be effective for the treatment of adults with IBS-C in two adequate and well controlled trials (Study 301 and Study 302) that were submitted with this application.

requirement.text: 3583-1: A 60-day, repeat-dose, GLP juvenile animal toxicology study in rats, dosing initiated on post-natal day 21.

citations.quote: 3583-1 A 60-day, repeat-dose, GLP juvenile animal toxicology study in rats in which the dosing of the animals should be initiated on post-natal day 21.

requirement.text: 3583-2: A randomized, double-blind, controlled, dose-ranging study of tenapanor for IBS-C in pediatric patients 6 to less than 12 years of age.

citations.quote: 3583-2 A randomized, double-blind, controlled, dose-ranging study to assess the safety and efficacy of tenapanor for the treatment of irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) in pediatric patients 6 to less than 12 years of age. The study will include at least 2 doses and treatment duration will be 4 weeks.

requirement.text: 3583-3: A 12-week, randomized, controlled study of tenapanor for IBS-C in pediatric patients 12 to less than 18 years of age.

citations.quote: 3583-3 A 12-week, randomized, controlled study to assess the safety and efficacy of tenapanor for the treatment of irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) in pediatric patients 12 to less than 18 years of age. The study will evaluate at least 2 doses.

requirement.text: 3583-4: A randomized, controlled study of tenapanor for IBS-C in pediatric patients 6 to less than 12 years of age.

citations.quote: 3583-4 A randomized, controlled study to assess the safety and efficacy of tenapanor for the treatment of irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) in pediatric patients 6 to less than 12 years of age.

requirement.text: 3583-5: An open-label, long-term extension study of tenapanor safety in pediatric patients 6 to less than 18 years of age who participated in study 3583-2, 3583-3, or 3583-4.

citations.quote: 3583-5 An open-label, long-term extension study to assess the safety of ongoing treatment with tenapanor for irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) in pediatric patients 6 to less than 18 years of age, who participated in study 3583-2, 3583-3, or 3583-4.

requirement.text: 3583-6: A milk-only lactation trial in lactating women receiving multiple twice-daily doses of tenapanor to assess concentrations of tenapanor (and its active metabolite) in breast milk (required under 505(o)).

citations.quote: 3583-6 A milk-only lactation trial in lactating women who have received multiple, twice daily, doses of tenapanor therapeutically to assess concentrations of tenapanor (and its active metabolite) in breast milk using a validated assay.
